task: Predict the forest cover type of a 30 m x 30 m cell in the Roosevelt National Forest, Colorado, from cartographic variables.
instructions: You are helping a feature-selection search for a classification task. Rate how useful each feature is likely to be for predicting the class, on its own or together with a few others, from 0 (useless) to 1 (most useful). Use only your knowledge of the domain and the descriptions given; you do not see the data. Reply with a JSON object only: {"scores": {"<feature index>": <score>, ...}} with one entry for every feature index listed.

calls.reply:
Feature names are anonymized, so I assume the standard covertype column order and score from that.

Assumed layout:
- 0: Elevation
- 1: Aspect
- 2: Slope
- 3: Horizontal distance to hydrology
- 4: Vertical distance to hydrology
- 5: Horizontal distance to roadways
- 6-8: Hillshade at 9am, noon and 3pm
- 9: Horizontal distance to fire points
- 10-13: Wilderness area (4 binary columns)
- 14-53: Soil type (40 binary columns)

Elevation is by far the strongest predictor. Horizontal distances to roadways and fire points come next, followed by the wilderness areas and the soil types that are most informative.

Soil indices are 14 + (soil type number − 1). I scored the soil types as follows:
- Soil types 2, 4, 10, 12, 22, 23, 29, 30, 38, 39 and 40 are the most informative, since they are common and tied to particular cover types.
- Soil 29 is index 42, soil 30 is index 43, soil 38 is index 51, soil 39 is index 52, and soil 40 is index 53.
- Soil 2 is index 15, soil 4 is index 17, soil 10 is index 23, soil 12 is index 25, soil 22 is index 35, and soil 23 is index 36.
- Other moderately useful ones are soil 6 (index 19), soil 13 (index 26), soil 17 (index 30), soil 20 (index 33), soil 24 (index 37), soil 31 (index 44), soil 32 (index 45), and soils 33 and 34 (indices 46 and 47).

Wilderness area 4 (index 13) is strongly tied to Ponderosa Pine and Cottonwood, and area 1 (index 10) is also informative.
